name: Past-conversation recall and isolation over synthetic cases
purpose: the labelled past conversation is among the three returned and no other user's conversation is, over synthetic cases Read in this direction: raise the rate at which the labelled past conversation is among the few returned, hold cross-user leakage at none, and keep the cost of a call bounded as the number of stored conversations grows. Only related_slices is driven (current_slice, filters, any database-backed ConversationStore and ClaudeConversationsAdapter are not), and case CNV-010 pins a paraphrase gap.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of each implementation on the same cases, with the recorded cost as the tie-break; each run is one row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash, and the leaderboard compares rows only when the hash matches.

name: Repeat-correction recall and precision over feedback sequences
purpose: repeat-correction rate on synthetic feedback sequences: after a correction is stored through the live ledger, does the guidance shown to the next relevant turn contain it (recall), and are corrections that do not bear on the turn kept out (precision). One component, feedback_loop, serves this row and store-feedback (many-to-one) Read in this direction: raise recall (a stored standing correction appears on the next relevant turn) and precision (irrelevant or one-off corrections stay out), lowering the repeat-correction rate. The guidance provider has no relevance cut below the card limit, so a stored rule that does not bear on a turn is shown while the limit has room (FL-06, FL-09, FL-10, FL-16). Corrections are surfaced when relevant, so the weakness is precision.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of each implementation on the same cases, with the recorded cost as the tie-break; each run is one row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash, and the leaderboard compares rows only when the hash matches.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the ledger_guidance offline arm of feedback_loop runs the whole case set with no model call]

name: Correction carry-through over the feedback-loop cases
purpose: the same feedback_loop component as guide-by-feedback (many-to-one): a correction recorded in the FeedbackLedger, a standing rule turned into a guidance card, a one-time request and an uncarded half of a mixed note kept out of guidance Read in this direction: lower the rate at which a person must repeat a correction. Only one FeedbackStore implementation exists (the file-backed ledger).
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of each implementation on the same cases, with the recorded cost as the tie-break; each run is one row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash, and the leaderboard compares rows only when the hash matches.
disadvantages: Its misses are guidance-selection precision, not storage; fidelity of the stored words is pinned by tests/test_feedback_ledger*.py.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the ledger_guidance offline arm of feedback_loop runs the whole case set with no model call]

purpose: warm start right over synthetic multi-turn cases, with no stale or cross-quest card returned Read in this direction: raise the share of follow-ups that get the right earlier cards. name: Prediction store contract pass rate
purpose: share of persistence contract scenarios (roundtrip, isolation, replace, expiry, view, clear, log, restart, tolerance) the store passes; a share held out Read in this direction: maximise exact round trip of saved data; maximise scope isolation; maximise correct expiry; maximise survival across a restart; ensure no store call raises. Backends differ in where data lives, not in how well they store it. Prediction quality is not measured at all: no case set replays recorded ask sequences through the anticipation engine, so nothing says how often a served prediction is right or what a wrong one costs.

name: Representative choice accuracy and thread consistency
purpose: Measures whether each request is handled by the representative that fits it and whether a thread keeps one representative. Read in this direction: maximise requests whose chosen representative matches the label; maximise spawned work that keeps its thread's representative; allow no selection by a bare mention or of a representative the person cannot see; minimise questions to the person and model calls.
record: Per implementation on the same labelled requests: the share matching the label, the share of spawned work keeping its thread's representative, selections by bare mention or of a hidden representative, questions asked, and model calls per choice; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet. The label of the right representative is the case author's judgment of fit; it cannot see whether the person would have preferred another; the host's chat classifier runs in the host, so its arm needs the host.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the persona_resolver_precedence offline arm of select_a_rep runs the whole case set with no model call]

name: Two-sided long-term guidance
purpose: Measures whether a reply points the person at the real next milestone and the real current reading at a natural moment, at the intent level that fits (goal, quest, or a representative's portfolio), after answering the request and briefly; and whether it holds back when the moment is wrong. Read in this direction: maximise nudge cases right and restraint cases right together (the value is their mean); allow no invented milestone or figure; allow no pointer in an urgent, narrow, unrelated, emotional or repeated case.
record: Per implementation on the same labelled cases: nudge cases right, restraint cases right, awkwardness on restraint cases, each per intent level (quest, goal, rep), and model calls per case, the grader's included; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: Twenty-four invented scenarios, so a first reading, not a population; the right level and the right moment are the case author's judgment; the grader is a model (sonnet through claude -p) and the reply model is the cheap tier, so the figures move with both.

name: Quest placement accuracy over labelled messages, balanced with cost and time
purpose: Measures whether a message is placed on exactly the quests it is about, or on none when no quest fits. Read in this direction: maximise the share of messages placed on exactly the labelled quests (none included) while a placement stays within its cost and time budgets. One number at every stage: accuracy, cost and time at the weights and budgets of [balance.place_on_a_quest], fixed before any arm was scored; an arm that spends the whole of a budget gets zero for it, so a model call has to buy its price in accuracy, and the library's judge, which sees only the quests in the order given, pays for that in accuracy on a large account. Case sources of the one number (none a stage, none with a pass test of its own): named quests, topics implied without the quest's words, vague cues resolved only by a milestone phrase, distractors that share words with the wrong quest, messages no quest fits, messages about two quests, and follow-ups that name nothing; plus real labelled messages where a machine holds them (QAR_PRIVATE_PLACEMENT_DATASET, at the share fixed in esoi.toml, absent means no case). The account is invented, a long list of quests of which a few are the ones the cases are about, with no Spiritual Data name.
record: Per implementation on the same cases: the exact-match rate, the right quest within the first three candidates, model calls, dollars and seconds per case, and the balanced number; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. Idea ratings of the descriptions (0 to 4 on the five questions of esoi/idea-rating-scale.md): shared-quest-ranker 3,3,3,4,4 (an embedding of the title alone cannot see milestones); hybrid-candidate-ranker 4,4,3,2,4 (costs an index read); library-quest-judge 2,2,3,4,4 (sees only the first quests it is given). The results are in evaluation/components/results.csv and the leaderboard of the cascade.
disadvantages: The first stage uses a local embedding model (bge-small) in place of the production embedding service, so its absolute numbers describe the ranking's shape, not production's. The public account is small and invented and the two model arms tie within noise, so the selection is a best guess, not significant; more cases with near-duplicate quests are the next thing to add. The index read the hybrid ranking needs per placement is not in the fixtures' time. The fixtures stand in for the database, so what the real data adds (notes, goals, entries) is only measured on the real source.
